answer: The network weaves a trellis of mutually‑signed credential shards, each shard anchored to a cryptographic crystal that timestamps the issuer’s reputation relic. When a new agent registers it must present a quorum of shards whose signatures form a linked‑proof chain; any duplicate identity cannot produce independent shards because the crystal’s nonce expires after one use. An attacker therefore must forge dozens of fresh credential shards and purchase corresponding crystal timestamps, inflating the cost to tens of thousands of tokens per fake node.
